episodes.157042: As thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze and pushed offshore in Brevard, a few produced strong wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.157205: Slow moving thunderstorms brought around 6 inches of rain in just a few hours to portions of Decatur county, resulting in flash flooding.  In addition, a few trees were blown down in portions of Colquitt and Worth counties.
episodes.157628: A surface front edging south across SE Georgia combined with a passing mid level short wave trough triggered a few strong to isolated severe storms over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.157629: A surface front edging south across SE Georgia combined with a passing mid level short wave trough triggered a few strong to isolated severe storms over a moist and unstable airmass.

episodes.157907: A weak trough was over the Rocky Mountains. A cold front from the previous day was across the Lower Trans Pecos which helped to provide atmospheric lift. High moisture and instability were present along the front. These conditions resulted in thunderstorms with large hail developing and moving across Terrell County in Texas.
episodes.158800: Severe thunderstorm moved through Corpus Christi around midnight with gusts to 60 mph occurring at the Corpus Christi Naval Air Station.
episodes.158808: Strong thunderstorms moved through the Coastal Bend during the evening hours of the 11th. The storms reached the coastal waters of the Middle Texas coast by late evening and continued into the early morning hours of the 12th. The storms produced wind gusts generally ranging from 35 to 45 knots with gusts up to 50 knots around Corpus Christi Naval Air Station.
episodes.158822: A cold front moved into the region during stalled during the morning of the 11th. Diurnal heating combined with high moisture and a disturbance aloft allowed scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop with some becoming severe.
episodes.158865: Tuesday night through Wednesday morning of May 11th into May 12th, a 500 mb shortwave trough worked from northwest to southeast from the Texas Big Bend through Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley, bringing a late-season cold front through the region. The Storm Prediction Center (SPC) forecasted a Marginal Risk of severe weather for the Rio Grande Plains/Brush Country and parts of the Lower Rio Grande Valley for this time period. While large hail was a potential threat, damaging winds took center stage as the squall line at the leading edge of the front tore through the Rio Grande Valley. Even more impressive was the strong, damaging winds behind the squall line associated with a ���wake low��� that lasted for several hours on the morning of May 12th. Later on during this event, some street flooding was observed in the San Benito area due to heavy rain.
episodes.158890: Early in the morning hours on May 12th, 2021, a stalled frontal boundary and associated mid-level disturbance helped to develop an eastward surging squall line across portions of southeastern Louisiana, resulting in damaging straight line winds and an isolated tornado.
episodes.158891: Early in the morning hours on May 12th, 2021, a stalled frontal boundary and associated mid-level disturbance helped to develop an eastward surging squall line across marine areas, resulting in severe wind gusts.
episodes.158916: A cold front moved to the coast causing scattered thunderstorms. A couple of high wind gusts were recorded.
episodes.158924: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front over South Central Texas for a third straight day. Some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.158951: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.158959: Strong thunderstorms developed over the western Florida panhandle and producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.159173: A moist and moderately unstable atmosphere along and ahead of a stationary front across central Georgia resulted in isolated strong to severe thunderstorms.

A tornado touched down between Claiborne Ave and Carrollton Ave in the Uptown area of New Orleans. It tracked east producing mostly tree and limb damage with a large tree uprooted near Napoleon Ave. It continued to track east producing tree damage before arriving near the Amtrak terminal and peeling back the tin roof on a large metal building. It tracked southeast, knocking down branches and trees in the Central Business District and then crossed the Mississippi River into Algiers. The tornado knocked down trees and power poles along with minor roof damage to a few homes and businesses before lifting near the Naval Support Activity Center.
